claims.text: Customer wants to browse and search products in the auction inventory by applying available filter/search criteria to find items of interest.
The system has auction inventory data populated and available for the 'Auctioneer' to access.

The Customer initiates the search by clicking the 'Go' button after entering a Product ID (e.g., ABC123) or Customer Email Address, or by selecting search parameters such as Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Product Type, and Cost Range, then clicking 'Find Product'.
Customer uses the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability to browse the auction inventory.
Customer selects a search/filter criterion, such as Product Type, from the scrolling list boxes; multiple filters may be selected simultaneously using the Control key.
Customer clicks the 'Find Product' button to execute the search based on the selected criteria.

System displays a table titled 'Search Results' containing columns for Action, Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, and Increment, with rows showing matching auction items.
The displayed results include thumbnail product images, and the Customer can sort the results by clicking the underlined column headers.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of using the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability, the Customer may enter the product browse/search experience via a Site Map page that lists all available Categories (Jewelry, Gemstones, Collectibles, Watches), Product Types (e.g., Rings, Necklaces, Bracelets), and Gemstone Types (e.g., Tanzanite, Diamond, Ruby) as direct links to specific pages or Endeca results pages.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of using the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability, the Customer may enter product browsing via SEO-optimized landing pages focused on specific gemstone types (e.g., a tanzanite page) or product types (e.g., a Rings page), which contain direct links to relevant product categories such as 'all loose tanzanite stones' or 'all tanzanite rings'.

Diverges from Step 2: Instead of selecting a search/filter criterion only from scrolling list boxes, the Customer may choose an inventory scope using radio buttons for 'Items currently online only' or 'All sellable auction inventory'; this selection does not impact the results of the 'Red status' columns.

Diverges from Step 2: Instead of selecting a search/filter criterion only from scrolling list boxes, the Customer may enable viewing items with or without images, or with or without a valid (sellable) location, via radio buttons; these filter options are combinable and alter the result set composition.
Diverges from Step 5: Instead of sorting by clicking underlined column headers, the Customer may sort the product results by 'Current Price: low to high' using a dropdown menu.
Diverges from Step 5: Instead of using the default result presentation, the Customer may switch between 'List View' and 'Catalog View' display modes for the product results.

Diverges from Step 5: Instead of only sorting the displayed results, the Customer may group the results using a scrolling list box with options including Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material, Material Purity, Product Group, Brand, Inventory Realm (Red, White), Inventory Aging Bucket, J/G Score, and Ring Size; each grouping option generates corresponding columns in the Results section.
Diverges from main_flow Step 1 (browse/navigation): If the Customer clicks a link that contains no product (e.g., Collectibles), the system serves a 'no results found' page.

Diverges from main_flow Step 3 (search execution): If the search results in no matches (e.g., for the term 'belly button'), the system displays a 'No Results Found' page containing (1) an apology/message stating no matches were found, (2) a 'Search Tips' section with five specific suggestions (check typos, remove unnecessary words, try plural/singular forms, use fewer/generic keywords, contact support), and (3) a 'May We Suggest'/'Popular Searches' section with static lists of popular gemstone and jewelry searches plus dynamically updated search terms/phrases using Omniture data. Exit: no results table is displayed; the Customer sees the No Results Found page.
Diverges from main_flow Step 3: The system excludes any matching items that lack an available image from appearing on product details pages, search results, or catalog pages.

The system has displayed a table titled 'Search Results' populated with rows for the auction items matching the Customer's selected browse/search/filter criteria; the table columns are, in default order: Action (checkbox), Item thumbnail image, Product ID (SKU #) with link to SKU History page, Auction ID, Description, Opening Bid, High Bid, Item Unit Cost, Start time (initially blank), End time (initially blank), Duration (initially blank), Product Type, and Increment.

When the search was performed for a Product ID, the system has displayed a 'Search Results for Item' section containing a table populated with rows from the matching auction history, with columns for Auction Status, Auction_Seq, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve, High Bid, # of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder.

The system has displayed a filtered product list in which each item is represented by a Product Module containing a thumbnail image, a short description (On-Air Description), a countdown timer in D:HH:MM:SS format showing time remaining, the current high bid, and a QuickBid button.
The Customer wants to complete checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.
The Customer has at least one unpaid won auction item for which checkout/payment has not yet been completed.
The Customer has previously chosen either PayPal or Amazon Payments as their default method of payment.
The Customer's account status (e.g., having won items) is a condition that must hold before successful checkout.

The Customer clicks a payment initiation link/button—such as the 'pay now' link in the winner notification email, the Winnings Alert link, or a 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button—to start checkout and payment.
The Customer chooses which won auction items to pay for from a list of won items by checking the 'Pay Now' checkbox next to each item.
The system offers the Customer a choice of shipping methods.
The Customer selects a shipping speed option (e.g., USPS Standard or Expedited) via radio buttons.
The Customer selects a checkout option by clicking one of three buttons: 'Check out with PayPal', 'Check out with Amazon', or 'Checkout Later'.
The system gets the Customer started on the payment process for their winnings.

Diverges from Step 4: Rather than selecting a checkout option, a returning Customer whose default Method of Payment is PayPal or Amazon Payments is routed to a specific page that offers a choice of shipping methods and initiates the payment process for their winnings.

Diverges from Step 4: The Customer may select PayPal as the payment method by choosing the corresponding radio button in the 'My Payment Methods' section, instead of using credit card or Amazon Payments.
Diverges from Step 4: The Customer may choose to pay using Amazon Payments, which opens a new browser session to register or log in, if they have purchased from Amazon in the past.

Diverges from Step 5: If PayPal is the Customer's default Method of Payment, the system sends an email notification upon winning an auction and the Customer must manually log into their JTV account to process payment within 7 days.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer already has a PayPal account, they may complete payment by logging in via the email and password fields on the right side of the page, rather than creating a new account or using Amazon.

Diverges from Step 5: The Customer may create a new PayPal account by selecting 'Create a PayPal account', entering Country (defaulted to United States), and choosing a payment method: either 'Bill Me Later®' or 'Credit Card'.

Diverges from Step 4: If the Customer clicks the 'Checkout Later' button or radio button, the system grays out the page, disables all links, and displays a DIV layer with specific text stating that payment can be made within 7 days (168 hours) but unpaid orders will be cancelled after the window expires.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer does not complete payment for the won item(s) within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time, the system cancels the unpaid order(s) and places the item(s) into 'Hold' status. Exit: the use case terminates without payment; the order(s) are cancelled.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer fails to complete the payment transaction within seven days (168 hours) of the auction's closing date/time, the email will include a notification that the Customer's account may be suspended.

Diverges from Step 5: If a PayPal or Amazon Payments Customer's unpaid order(s) are more than 7 days old (expired/unresolved auction winnings), the system automatically locks the Customer's account and puts it into 'Review Status'; because the order(s) are already cancelled, the Customer cannot unlock the account by paying for them. Exit: the use case terminates without payment; the account is in Review Status and cannot be unlocked by the Customer's payment.
The 'Payment Status' column in the 'Items I've Won' table displays 'Paid' for items where the transaction has been successfully completed.

After the Customer completes the Amazon or PayPal checkout process, the Customer is returned to a Thank You page that uses the global header and footer and includes a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.

Customer manages their account settings by updating their membership account information (e.g., first name, last name, member ID, email address, phone, password) and managing email notification preferences.
The Customer is authenticated (logged in) to the system.
The Customer has an existing account with registration information (First Name, Last Name, Member ID, E-mail Address, Phone) and a current password already stored in the system.
The Customer navigates to the 'Change Membership Account Information' page (the My Account Edit Page) to update their stored membership account information.

The Customer views the 'My Current Information' section, which displays their existing First Name, Last Name, Member ID ('Handle'), E-mail Address, Phone, and requires entry of the Current Password to authorize changes.
The Customer enters their Current Password to authorize changes.

The Customer enters updated information into the 'My New Information' section fields: First Name, Last Name, Member ID ('Handle'), E-mail Address (entered twice for verification), Phone, and Password (entered twice for verification).
The Customer manages email notification preferences by checking the desired boxes: notify me via email when I am outbid, notify me when I win an auction, and notify me when my winnings are shipped.
The Customer clicks the 'Save Changes' button to submit their updates.
Upon saving changes, the Customer is returned to the My Account page.

Diverges from Step 4: Instead of using the notification checkboxes to manage email preferences, the Customer may click the 'Change my "Auction Insider" Email Newsletter Subscription' link to opt out of the 'Auction Insider' newsletter subscription.
Diverges from Step 4: If the Customer has chosen PayPal or Amazon as their payment type, the 'Please notify me when I win an auction' checkbox is grayed out, so the Customer may not de-select it.

Diverges from Step 5: Instead of clicking the 'Save Changes' button, the Customer may click the red 'Cancel' button; the system discards any entered changes and immediately returns the Customer to the My Account page without saving changes.
Diverges from Step 2: If the Customer does not complete the current-password authorization step, the system prevents modification of the account information.
Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer submits an email address that is not unique in the customer table, the system treats the duplicate as an error condition requiring correction.
Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer enters a password outside the required 8 to 12 character range, the system triggers a validation error and prevents the save.
Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer's two password entries do not match, the system rejects the save.
Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer attempts to set a Member ID ('Handle') that is not unique in the customer table, the system returns an error state.
The Customer's updated membership account information (First Name, Last Name, Member ID, E-mail Address, Phone, Password) is saved to the system and persisted.

The Customer's selected email notification preferences ('notify me when I am outbid', 'notify me when I win an auction', 'notify me when my winnings are shipped') are saved and will govern future transactional email behavior.
After saving changes, the Customer is returned to the My Account page.

Customer wants to monitor the current and past auction status of a product item, including its auction status (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed), dates/times, bid counts, and winning bidder information.

The user has access to the relevant auction status monitoring/reporting page: either through an authenticated Auctioneer session in the Auction Admin Application while in the Auction Admin Main Menu workspace (e.g., Current Auctions Status Page), or through the customer-facing Product Details page for the product item (with Item Bid History showing current high bid, open/close times, and past bids).
The target customer history view has been identified using at least one of Customer Email Address, Customer Home Phone, or Customer Name (Last, First).
Customer initiates the auction status view for a specific product item by entering the Product ID and clicking “Go.”
User initiates the auction status/history view for a specific product item by entering the Product ID and clicking “Go.”
The system displays the search results in two sections: a top section showing product summary data and a bottom section listing the item's auction history data on separate lines.
The system lists each individual auction record with its Auction Status, Auction Sequence, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve Amount, High Bid, Number of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder.

The user clicks the Winner/High Bidder link to open the customer's history page, selects the 'Bid History' button; the system displays the Bid History section, including closing date/time (or 'Active' for live auctions), auction sequence numbers, product ID (SKU), the customer's last bid, their SmartBid (max bid), and the winning bid. The user opens the Product Details page for the item, which displays the Item Bid History table showing Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User status.
Diverges from Step 4: If an auction is still live, the Bid History section displays 'Active' instead of a closing date/time for that auction; if the auction is closed, its closing date/time is shown.
Diverges from Step 4: The Bid History section includes the customer's SmartBid (max bid) amount if one was placed on the auction.
Diverges from Step 2: The page provides a 'Recently Ended Auctions' link; if the customer selects it, the system displays the last 24 hours of auction history as an alternative viewing scope.

If a search results in no matches (No Results Found), the system displays a 'No Results' page which includes a 'Search Tips' section with specific advice: check for typos/misspellings, remove unnecessary words like 'and', 'the', or 'a', try plural and singular forms of the word, use fewer or more generic keywords, and contact support if tips fail.

The system displays the specified product item's current and past auction status history in two sections: a top product summary section and a bottom section listing each auction history record on a separate line.

Each auction history record in the bottom section shows Auction Status, Auction Sequence, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve Amount (Opening Bid), High Bid, Number of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder.

The Bid History section lists each auction record with its closing date/time (or 'Active' for a live auction), auction sequence number, product ID (SKU), the customer's last bid, the SmartBid if one was placed, and the winning bid (regardless of who placed it).
The Item Bid History section lists, for each bid, the bidder's Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User? status.
The Customer wants to place a bid on an auction item.
The Customer is signed in.
The Customer has agreed to be bound by the Terms of Use Agreement.
The Customer has a valid payment method (credit card) on file.
The Customer clicks the 'QuickBid Now' button, or selects an amount and clicks the 'Place SmartBid' or 'Place Single Bid' button, to place a bid.
The Customer selects an amount and clicks the 'Place SmartBid' or 'Place Single Bid' button, or clicks the 'QuickBid Now' button to place a single bid.

The system checks the bidder's sign-in status and bidder eligibility (no unresolved unpaid auction winnings older than 7 days, and not on review status under the escalation policy) before allowing the bid to be placed.

The system displays a 'Bid Confirmation Pop-up' asking for verification of the amount and card details, and showing the bid amount, bid type, and payment method, with 'Yes, Place [Type] Bid' and 'Cancel' buttons.
The Customer confirms the bid by clicking the 'Yes, Place [Type] Bid' button (e.g., 'Yes, Place SmartBid').
The system processes the bid.
The Customer remains on the product details page.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of selecting an amount from the 'Your SmartBid' or 'Your Single Bid' dropdown and clicking 'Place SmartBid'/'Place Single Bid', the Customer clicks the 'QuickBid Now' button, which uses the value in the 'QuickBid Amount' field; the system places a single bid and skips the confirmation popup.

Diverges from Step 1: The Customer can place a bid directly from the catalog view by clicking the 'QuickBid' button located under each item's price and timer, or from the Category Page List View by clicking the 'QuickBid' button next to an item.
Diverges from Step 1: The Customer can access bidding options via the 'SmartBid' button located on the Category Page List View.

Diverges from Step 2: The system checks the bidder's sign-in status and finds that the Customer is not signed in. The system takes the Customer directly to the sign-in page. After the sign-in process, if the Customer has the required minimum information required to bid, the system returns the Customer to the product details page of the item they initially tried to bid on; the bid is not placed, and the exception branch ends with the Customer on the product details page. If the Customer has signed in but lacks the required minimum information required to bid, the system returns the Customer to the product details page rather than accepting the bid, so the bid is not placed.

Diverges from Step 4: The Customer clicks the 'CANCEL' button in the bid confirmation popup, canceling the bid confirmation process. This prevents the bid from being placed and terminates this exception branch.
The Customer's bid has been placed; the system records it in the 'Item Bid History' table with the bidder's Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User status.
The Customer remains on the Product Details Page of the auction item after the bid is placed, rather than being redirected to a confirmation or checkout page.
The system updates the 'Current High Bid' dynamically for all items without requiring a page refresh.
The bid is recorded to 1/100th of a second.
The Customer's 'My Watch List' page displays the item with updated 'Current High Bid', 'Total Bids', 'Last Bid Time', and 'Ending Time'.
A new customer wants to create a free JTVauctions.com membership account.

The user has access to a valid email address and phone number.

Diverges from Step 5: If the customer selects Credit Card as the payment method, the customer provides the corresponding billing details.

Diverges from Step 8: When a new customer tries to create an account, the system cross-references the Consumer Protection negative file; if there is a match, the registrant receives the message: 'We are sorry, we are unable to create an auction account for you at this time. If you believe this message to be in error, please contact our Customer Service team at: 800-550-8393.' No auction account is created.

After the registration process is completed (either via short or full registration), the system displays a 'Welcome Back!' message and presents the Sign In page with fields for Member ID/Email and Password.

If the customer completed the short registration by clicking the 'I Want to Sign in Now!' button, the system takes them to the sign-in page and, if they were previously browsing before registering, returns them to their last product details page (or the home page if they were on it).

The system triggers an automated transactional email containing a 'Thank You' message for registering and instructions to enable cookies and add the appropriate email address(es) to the customer's whitelist/Safe Senders list.
If the customer provided optional billing/shipping addresses and shipping preferences for the account, the system saves them to the customer's account profile.

If registration is completed via the 'Save Changes' button, the system displays a pop-up message instructing the user to add shop@jewelryTV.rsys1.com to their address book or safe senders list and to enable cookies in their browser.
The Customer wants to cancel a bid during an auction.
The Customer has a confirmed bid on an item in an auction that is currently active (the auction has not yet ended).
The Customer attempts to cancel a bid during an auction.
If the Customer attempts to retract a confirmed bid, the system rejects the attempt because auction bids may not be cancelled; the retraction is not performed and the confirmed bid remains in effect.

If a bid retraction is not possible because the auction has ended or the bid was already superseded by a higher bid, the system displays an error message to the Customer indicating that the bid cannot be retracted.
The system prevents bid retraction if the user is currently the highest bidder on an item.
The confirmed bid is cancelled and removed from effect.
The retracted bid is removed from the item's current bidding history.
If the retracted bid was the displayed high bid, the displayed high bidder is updated to reflect the next highest valid bid.
The Customer offers a cancelled item to the second-place finisher at the second-place finisher's last bid price.
There is a winning order that has not been paid for with Amazon or PayPal within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time and is therefore cancelled and placed in 'Hold' status.
There is a second-place finisher available for the specific auction item of the cancelled winning order.

The use case begins when a second-chance offer is triggered for a winning order that has already been cancelled and placed into 'hold' status; the original cancellation is a completed precondition and remains outside this use case.
The system sends an automated email to the second-place finisher for the cancelled winning order.
The email offers to sell the cancelled item to the second-place finisher at the second-place finisher's last bid price.
The email presents the second-place finisher with three response options: Credit Card Option, PayPal or Amazon Payments Option, or Decline Option (the 'No Thanks' button).
At main_flow step 1, if the second-place finisher's bid is below the item's unit cost, the system does not send the 2nd-Chance email.
At main_flow step 1, if the 2nd-Chance recipient has two accounts and is essentially bidding against themselves, the system does not send the 2nd-Chance email.

At main_flow step 1, if matches are found between the 2nd-Chance recipient's account data and the winner's account data on any of Customer Name, Customer Phone Number, Customer Email Address, Customer Member ID, or Customer Billing and/or Shipping Addresses, the system does not send the 2nd-Chance email.

At main_flow step 3, if the second-place finisher does not respond to the 2nd-Chance email within 72 hours after the email is sent, the item is returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction.
An automated 2nd-Chance email has been sent to the second-place finisher, offering the cancelled winning order at the second-place finisher's last bid price.

The C2 JU wants to define reference points and geometric areas (including segmented lines, multisided areas, squares, rectangles, circles, ellipses, corridors, low-level transit routes, slaved points/areas, and areas of probability) by transmitting data reports with the specific field values and indicators for the chosen type.
The C2 JU is participating in the exchange of J3 Surveillance messages and uses Network PGs for surveillance information.
For a slaved reference point or geometric area, a Related TN exists to which the point or area is slaved in a constant position.

For an Area of Probability (AOP), the C2 JU is capable of generating and maintaining track numbers and has a basis from organic data, exchanged lines of bearing (LOBs), analysis of EW fix data, or a combination of these.

The trigger is the need to define or report any in-scope reference point or geometric area (including, for example, corridors and low-level transit routes), initiated when the C2 JU transmits a data report (e.g., a J3.0 or J3.5 (PTI = 0) original message) containing the specific field values and indicators for the selected type. This includes the need to report a ballistic missile launch point or impact point, and, for an Area of Probability, the C2 JU generating and maintaining track numbers based on organic data, exchange of LOBs, analysis of EW fix data, or a combination of these.
The C2 JU selects the type of reference point or geometric area to define and the corresponding J3.0 data report format to use (J3.0 supports points, lines, areas, and volumes such as corridors).
The C2 JU assigns a Track Number (TN) to each point/line/area being defined.

The C2 JU populates the J3.0 message with the field values and indicators required for the selected type, for example the Point/Line/Area Descriptor; Point Type and Point Amplification; and, for an Area of Probability, the Square/Circle Switch, Axis Orientation, and Area Major/Minor Axis fields.

The C2 JU reports the position: for non-slaved reference points/geometric areas, using geodetic latitude/longitude values, and includes altitude/elevation if required; for slaved reference points/areas, when the Slaved Indicator is set to value 1, the position is established as Delta Latitude/Delta Longitude from the Related TN instead of absolute geodetic latitude/longitude.
The C2 JU reports the time associated with the entity in hours/minutes as defined by the Time Function field.

The reporting JU transmits the J3.0 message defining the reference point or geometric area; for a segmented line or multisided area described by more than 3 points, the reporting JU also transmits subsequent J3.0 messages, each with a unique TN, with the Line/Area Continuation Indicator set to value 1, with the point location in each subsequent message coincident with the last point described in the previous word sequence, closing a multisided area by making its last transmitted point identical to the initial point, and the Reference TN of the first J3.0 message with Line/Area Continuation Indicator set to value 0 is used as the only legal identifier for all subsequent references to the segmented line or multisided area.

Diverges from Step 1: if the selected reference point is an emergency point, the C2 JU transmits a J3.1 message to report the emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts instead of a J3.0 data report; if related to a previously reported track/point, the J3.1 message includes the associated Track Number (TN) as amplifying information and the emergency point must have a TN different from the previously reported TN; if the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1, the report is for exercise purposes and not an actual emergency.
Diverges from Step 3: when the J3.0 message is used to report a point, the C2 JU sets the Point/Line/Area Descriptor field (field 1) to value 0 (Point) in the initial word.

Diverges from Step 3: when joining 2 or 3 points to form a segmented line, the C2 JU sets the Line/Area Continuation Indicator to 'No Statement' in the initial word, sets the End Point field to value 1, sets the Point/Line/Area Descriptor to value 2 (Line), and uses Delta Latitude/Longitude fields relative to the designated reference point.

Diverges from Step 3: when defining a square or rectangle (Square/Circle Switch = 1) or a circle or ellipse (Square/Circle Switch = 2), the C2 JU sets the Point/Line/Area Descriptor field in the J3.0I word to value 1 (Single Point Area).
Diverges from Step 3: when reporting a moving point, line, or area, the C2 JU sets Course and Speed in the J3.0C2 word to values other than No Statement.

Diverges from Step 4: as an alternative to absolute positioning, the C2 JU may define certain reference points and areas as 'slaved' in a constant position relative to a Related TN by setting the Slaved Indicator to value 1 and establishing position via Delta Latitude/Longitude; if the J3.0C4 word is included, the bearing is relative to the course of the Related TN, otherwise it is a constant true bearing; lines and irregular multisided areas (other than squares, rectangles, circles, and ellipses) shall not be slaved.
Diverges from Step 4: when describing a multisided area, the last point location transmitted must be the same location as the initial point transmitted in the first word sequence to close the figure.

Diverges from Step 6: when joining more than 3 points to form a segmented line or multisided area, the C2 JU transmits multiple J3.0 messages, setting the Line/Area Continuation Indicator to value 1 (Continuation) in the second and subsequent messages, with the point location in the extension word matching the last point of the previous message.

Diverges from Step 6: when a segmented line or multisided area is already defined and data concerning any point comprising a portion of the entity changes, the C2 JU transmits the entire line or area rather than only the changed point.

Diverges from main flow Step 2: if the C2 JU attempts to assign a Reference TN that already identifies a particular reference or emergency point to any other type of surveillance entity reported on the interface, the action is illegal; the Reference TN shall not be used for any other entity type except in the normal course of TN reuse.

Diverges from main flow Step 2: if the C2 JU attempts to use a Reference TN other than the Reference TN of the first J3.0 message with Line/Area Continuation Indicator set to value 0 for subsequent references to a segmented line or multisided area, that attempt is not legal; the first message's Reference TN is the only legal identifier for all subsequent references, except for dropping the line/area, setting/clearing the Force Tell Indicator, or responding to a Data Update Request by TN.

Diverges from main flow Step 3: if the C2 JU attempts to change the Point Type and/or Point Amplification value of a reference point while retaining the same Reference TN, the change is illegal; the only permitted exception is changing a Point Amplification value of No Statement to a non-No Statement value while retaining the same Reference TN.

The C2 JU has a requirement to filter data based on specific criteria.
The C2 JU has determined the type of filter required (e.g., Reference Point, Geometric Area) and its associated parameters (e.g., latitude/longitude, shape, size).
The C2 JU has assigned a unique Filter Number (a value between 1 and 14) to identify the new filter definition.
The C2 JU needs to exchange tactical information about geographic references or report the location of fixed ground units or objects.
The C² JU initiates the definition or maintenance of a reference point, line, or area by assuming Reporting Responsibility ($R^2$).
To establish or update the reference point, line, or area, the C² JU transmits a J3.0 Reference Point message containing the relevant data.
If defining a segmented line or multisided area, the C² JU transmits J3.0 messages for each Reference TN used to define the geometry.
If time association is required (e.g., establishment, activation), the C² JU reports the Time and Time Function in the first Reference TN message, which applies to the entire line or area.
All receiving JUs accept the alert or data contained in the J3.0 message into their databases.

If a JU with R² needs to initiate a force tell alert on a reference point, line, or area, it sets the FT IND in the J3.0 Reference Point message; termination is done by transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 4) message or setting FT IND to 0.

When reporting a ballistic missile Launch Point or Impact Point, the J3.0 message is used with specific Time Function values (e.g., Departure Time or Arrival Time), and if related to a specific track, it is identified in the Related 2 Track Number field.
If a Drop Track Report is received for a ballistic missile, the JU with R² of the Launch Point or Impact Point transmits the point messages with the Connect/Disconnect field set to Disconnect.

For exercise purposes, the Exercise Indicator in the J3.0 message is set to amplify messages for Area (Hazard) or Missile Engagement Zones (MEZ) to indicate they are not for actual operational engagement.
It is a system option to retain the TN and last reported position of a fixed land IU that has reverted to an inactive status.

If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track Report message is received, the R² unit is declared inactive, or if no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another IU may, by operator action only, assume R² for the point using the same Reference TN.

The C2 JU defines reference points and geometric areas by exchanging J3.0 Reference Point messages that report geographic references (e.g., waypoints, CAP stations, FEBA) and by connecting and closing plotted points to form the specified geometric area.
Each point, line, or area reported on the interface shall be assigned a TN(s) by the reporting JU.
Multiple J3.0 messages, each with a unique TN, are used to define segmented lines or multisided areas described by more than 3 points.
The C2 JU receives a J7.1 (ACT = 0) Data Update Request by Request Indicator message with the Reference Point Data Request Indicator set to value 1.

The C2 JU which originated the data, or which has R2 for a J3.0 multi-point area or multi-segmented line (defined by more than one J3.0 message), provides the response messages required when the Reference Point Data Request Indicator is set to value 1.

The C2 JU originates a J3.0 Reference Point message to exchange tactical information about geographic references (nonphysical points such as waypoints, Combat Air Patrol (CAP) stations, Forward Edge of the Battle Area (FEBA)).
The C2 JU reports a point, line, or area on the interface and assigns a TN(s) to each reported point, line, or area.
The C2 JU defines a multi-point area or multi-segmented line using more than one J3.0 message.
When describing a segmented line, the C2 JU sets the Point/Line/Area Descriptor, 1 field in the initial word to value 2, Line.
When describing a multisided area, the C2 JU sets the Point/Line/Area Descriptor, 1 field in the initial word to value 3, Multi-point Area.

When defining a square, rectangle, circle, or ellipse, the C2 JU uses a J3.0I/J3.0E0/J3.0C2 word sequence and sets the Point/Line/Area Descriptor, 1 field in the J3.0I word to value 1, Single Point Area.

The C2 JU uses the Latitude and Longitude fields in the J3.0E0 word as the designated reference point from which Delta Latitude 1, Delta Longitude 1, Delta Latitude 2, and Delta Longitude 2 are measured.

When joining three or more points to form a segmented line, the C2 JU plots the points and connects the segments in sequence; the first segment is drawn from the point described in the Latitude and Longitude fields in the J3.0E0 word to the point established by the Delta Latitude 1 and Delta Longitude 1 fields in the J3.0C1 word.
To form an area, the C2 JU transmits the last point location as the same location as the initial point transmitted in the first word sequence, closing the figure to form an area.

If 2 or 3 points are joined together to form a segmented line, a single J3.0 message is used; the Line/Area Continuation Indicator is set to No Statement in the initial word, and the Point/Line/Area Descriptor, 1 field is set to value 2, Line.
If the segmented line or multisided area is moving, the C2 JU adds a J3.0C2 word to the first message.
Alternatively, when defining an area that is a square, rectangle, circle, or ellipse, a J3.5I/J3.5E0/J3.5C3 or a J3.7I/J3.7C1/J3.7C2 word sequence is used.

If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received, the R2 unit is declared inactive, or if no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may, by operator action only, assume R2 for the point, line, or area using the same Reference TN(s).

If a JU without R2 desires that a specific point, line, or area be transmitted immediately without awaiting the next periodic update, it should transmit a J7.1 (ACT = 1) Data Update Request for the desired TN.

If a JU without R2 initiates or terminates a force tell alert on a segmented line or multisided area, it shall set/clear the FT IND in a J7.0 (ACT = 4) message for each Reference TN which has been used to report the line or area; upon receipt, the JU with R2 shall set/clear the FT IND in all J3.0 messages used to report the line or area.
Exceptions to the normal point, line, or area reporting requirement apply when dropping the line or area, setting/clearing the Force Tell Indicator, or responding to a Data Update Request by TN.

If IFF/SIF data are available, the J3.1 message contains IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes); in the case of an emergency point initiated for a previously reported track, those data contain the IFF/SIF modes and codes of that previously reported track.

The System Operator initiates reporting through operator action only when the JU has additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point, or when a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received or no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals.

If a JU without R² desires that a specific point, line, or area be transmitted immediately without awaiting the next periodic update, it should transmit a J7.1 (ACT = 1) Data Update Request for the desired TN.
If a JU fails to receive the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and further updates are not received, the JU may purge those points after a specified time period has elapsed with no updates.
A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a point, line, or area shall not be required to purge the point, line, or area.

However, if the JU does not purge a point, line, or area on which it has received a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, it shall assume R² for the point, line, or area to ensure that it remains active on the interface.
A JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a point when the point becomes an Active IU on the interface with the same TN.
When a remote point, line, or area is purged from a system by local options, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.
